item.name: Beginner Spearfishing Course
item.description:
Learn the basics of becoming a safe and effective underwater hunter in our full day course!

*Disclaimer: There is no course that will immediately make you a top tier spearo or speara because it is a sport that requires time and repetition. However, you can learn techniques that will greatly increase your hunting success, and more importantly the factors to keep at the forefront in order to keep yourself safe in a dynamic environment.

The whole day will be spent on our 40' trawler Escapade as we head to the Coronado Islands for its clearer water (usually 10-20' better visibility than coastal San Diego), abundant life, and excellent structure from 5' deep to 60' deep and beyond. On the 3 hour trip out we will cover spearfishing technique and theory, gun familiarization, fish ID, etc. At the islands we will go through some rescues and safety protocols, set up a target to practice loading and shooting, develop fish ID while diving with the gun unloaded, and finish off with some full on hunting. On the way back we will break out the filet table and get some practice caring for our catch, and might even make some ceviche for the drive back!

Our guides are certified freediving instructors who have a passion for spearfishing, and the experience to go with it. Over the years of teaching spearfishing to hundreds of students, our team has found a student to instructor ratio of 3:1 is the maximum to be safe and effective. This means you will get a lot of personalized instruction with someone who is keeping an eye out for safety and is professionally trained to help you improve all aspects of your freediving and hunting techniques. We hand pick our instructors and are obnoxiously selective because in addition to being a skilled diver and hunter, we look for instructors who are personable and able to determine the needs of each individual student. They are also a ton of fun

Pre-Requisites:

The biggest factor in spearfishing is your ability to freedive. You don't have to dive deep, but you need to be comfortable in open water, kicking long distances on the surface, and making smooth dives consistently. If any of these are a challenge, adding hunting with a loaded weapon to the equation is overwhelming at best, and at worst a safety risk to yourself and the others around. Because of this, taking a Beginner Freediver Course is a mandatory pre-requisite. It doesn't have to be through our shop, as long as it is through a reputable agency you are all set (Molchanovs/FII/PFI/PADI/AIDA/SSI). While the best option is to do a freediving course separately, we do offer a combination Beginner Freediver + Spearfishing Course if you want to go that route. We have found this to be too much to absorb for people brand new to the sport, but if you have experience this can be a good option. These are found under our Beginner Freediver Course, with the option to select W1 + Spear at checkout. 

Over the past 4 years our team has taught over 1000 students and put what we have learned into our program. Here are a few things that differentiate us from many other freediving schools.

Included: Classroom instruction, captain and guide, charter to Coronado Islands with fuel included

Not Included: Passport, Mexican Fishing License (~$15 for 1 day), dive gear, spearfishing gear, fish processing, food and drinks

Equipment

A 5mm 2 piece freediving wetsuit is required, along with fins, mask, snorkel, and a weight belt with ~12lbs of weight. Booties and gloves recommended. All gear can be rented through Just Get Wet at a cost of $50 for the full kit per day (if taking the combo course it's $80 for the course duration)
A speargun and a knife. Available for rent from JGW for $50

Schedule:

7AM - 6PM
item.booking_notes:
Hi there,

Please take a moment to review the information below, including important details about scheduling, gear rentals, and preparation.

**Cancellation Policy** Please note that we have a strict refund, reschedule, and cancellation policy with no exceptions, as outlined on our website. You can review the policy [here](https://justgetwet.com/pages/cancellation-policies).

Gear rental information is included below further on in this email.

##Where to Meet & Park

**Meeting Location**
Dana Landing Fuel Dock, located right behind the tackle shop
2580 Ingraham St, San Diego, CA 92109

Please meet at the picnic tables behind the tackle shop with everything ready to load onto the boat. The shop has a deli, snacks, drinks, and you can get your fishing license there.

**Parking Notes**

-Do not park in front of the tackle shop (not for charters)
-You can park on the street next the tackle shop parking lot
-Additional options include the boat launch parking lot or the Northern Parking Lot (search “Freedom Boat Club”)
 
![Description of image](https://cdn.filestackcontent.com/4VXzrmBwQnKVewiZS7q1)    

##Schedule
6:45 AM
Be ready to walk down to the Dana Landing Fuel Dock with all gear, snacks, drinks, and required documentation. We will load the boat promptly so we can depart at 7:00 AM.
7:00 AM–9:30 AM
Transit to Coronado Islands, spearfishing theory, gun familiarization, fish ID, and regulations
9:30 AM–3:00 PM
Dive Technique Practice, Target practice, hunting technique, and spearfishing
3:00 PM–5:30 PM
Fish fillet class during transit back to dock

##Spearfishing Requirements

**Valid Passport**
You will need to bring your passport with you!

**Mexican Fishing License**
You will also need a MX Fishing License, which you can get [here] (https://www.mexpermits.com/).

**California Fishing License**
You will need a valid CA fishing license. Licenses can be purchased online or in person at bait and tackle shops, Walmart, Dick’s Sporting Goods, or directly at the Dana Landing Fuel Dock.

We recommend purchasing your license 1–2 days before the trip, in case weather or minimum bookings prevent the outing from running. If you do not hear from us, plan for the Coronado Islands!                   

##Boat & What to Bring

-Keep gear minimal and use soft gear bags only
-No hard cases or wheeled bags (not allowed onboard)
-Sunscreen, hat, sunglasses
-Warm outer layer or parka for transits (Surf Fur parkas available on boat)
-Bring plenty of water, a lunch, and snacks

##Equipment Requirements

All required equipment can be rented from Just Get Wet. If you need to rent gear, you will have to do so ahead of time and pick up your gear the day prior, except for spearguns which we keep on the boat. **Spearguns are included in the price of the course**. If you have your own to bring that's even better!

**Required**

-Mask/Snorkel
-5mm wetsuit - highly recommend two-piece open-cell freediving or spearfishing wetsuit for San Diego
-Longblade freediving fins (No split fins or open-heel bootie fins)
-Weight belt (rubber preferred)
-12 lbs of weights

##Insurance & Seasickness

We strongly recommend DAN dive accident insurance:
https://dan.org/membership-insurance/dive-insurance/

If prone to seasickness, begin Dramamine the night before open water and eat something small and bland (avoid citrus)

If you have any questions, feel free to reach out:
info@justgetwet.com
619-320-8022 (call or text)

We’re looking forward to diving with you!

Cheers,
Just Get Wet Crew

start_location.name: Dana Landing Fuel Dock
start_location.note: Search for the Dana Landing Bait and Tackle Shop. The Fuel dock is right behind it, and that is where the boat will be waiting. Do not park in the parking lot at the tackle shop! You can park on the street, right in front of that parking lot, which will be the closest place to the fuel dock. There is also a small parking lot just to the north of the tackle shop, if you search for Freedom Boat Club it will take you to this lot. You can also park here, and this is the preferred place to park for overnight trips.
